examples.question_text:
a. Which ribbon is longer: $1.37$ m or $139$ cm?
b. A student says $1370$ mm is longer than $1.37$ m because $1370>1.37$. Correct the claim.
examples.solution_text:
a. Use centimetres.
$1.37\times100=137$
$1.37\text{ m}=137\text{ cm}$
$137\text{ cm}<139\text{ cm}$
The $139$ cm ribbon is longer.
b. Use millimetres.
$1.37\times100\times10=1370$
$1.37\text{ m}=1370\text{ mm}$
The lengths are equal. Compare the numbers only after using the same unit.

examples.question_text: Order these walking routes from shortest to longest: $1.238$ km, $1260$ m, $1$ km $245$ m and $1.251$ km.
examples.solution_text:
Use metres for all four routes.
$1.238\times1000=1238$
$1.238\text{ km}=1238\text{ m}$
$1\text{ km }245\text{ m}=1000\text{ m}+245\text{ m}=1245\text{ m}$
$1.251\times1000=1251$
$1.251\text{ km}=1251\text{ m}$
$1238<1245<1251<1260$
Shortest to longest: $1.238\text{ km},\ 1\text{ km }245\text{ m},\ 1.251\text{ km},\ 1260\text{ m}$.

examples.question_text: Which lengths are greater than $1.5$ m: $149$ cm, $1500$ mm, $1.503$ m and $0.00152$ km?
examples.solution_text:
Use millimetres, including for the $1.5$ m comparison length.
$1.5\text{ m}=1.5\times1000\text{ mm}=1500\text{ mm}$
$149\text{ cm}=149\times10\text{ mm}=1490\text{ mm}$
$1.503\text{ m}=1.503\times1000\text{ mm}=1503\text{ mm}$
$0.00152\text{ km}=0.00152\times1000\text{ m}=1.52\text{ m}$
$1.52\text{ m}=1.52\times1000\text{ mm}=1520\text{ mm}$
$1490<1500$, $1500=1500$, $1503>1500$ and $1520>1500$.
The lengths greater than $1.5$ m are $1.503$ m and $0.00152$ km. The $1500$ mm length is equal, so it is not included.

examples.question_text: Which distance is longest: $0.1426$ km, $143$ m, $14280$ cm or $142900$ mm?
examples.solution_text:
Use metres for all four distances.
$0.1426\text{ km}=0.1426\times1000\text{ m}=142.6\text{ m}$
$143\text{ m}=143\text{ m}$
$14280\text{ cm}=14280\div100\text{ m}=142.8\text{ m}$
$142900\text{ mm}=142900\div10\div100\text{ m}=142.9\text{ m}$
$143>142.9>142.8>142.6$
The $143$ m distance is longest.
